title.en: Sole proprietorship and Joint Hindu Family business

hook.en: The corner shop, the tailor, the tea stall: most businesses in India are owned by one person. Some are run by a whole family under its eldest member.

objectives.en: Explain the features, merits and limitations of sole proprietorship
Explain the Joint Hindu Family business and the role of the Karta

narration.en: The corner shop, the tailor, the tea stall: most businesses in India are owned by one person. Some are run by a whole family under its eldest member.

body.en: A sole proprietorship is owned, managed and controlled by one person, who takes all the profit and bears all the risk. It is easy to form and close (few legal formalities), the owner has sole control and quick decisions, business secrets stay private, and the owner has a direct personal touch with customers. But the owner has unlimited liability (personal property can be used to pay business debts), limited capital and managerial skill, and the business has no separate legal entity and limited life: it may end with the owner's death, insolvency or illness.

points.en: One owner: all profit, all risk
Easy to form; quick decisions; secrecy

title.en: On the board: Joint Hindu Family (HUF) business

say.en: A business owned by the members of a Hindu Undivided Family, governed by Hindu law.

text.en: Membership by birth in the family (coparceners)
Managed by the eldest member: the Karta
Other coparceners: liability limited to their share
Continues after the Karta's death; the next eldest takes
Mitakshara (most of India) and Dayabhaga (West Bengal)
Since 2005, daughters are also coparceners by birth

body.en: Both forms are easy to run and are found mainly in small businesses. A sole proprietorship is formed by the will of one person; an HUF business arises by operation of Hindu law. The sole trader has unlimited liability; in an HUF only the Karta does, while coparceners are liable only to the extent of their share. An HUF continues after the death of the Karta, giving it more stability, but the Karta's dominance and limited capital are drawbacks. Neither has a separate legal entity.

points.en: Sole: by will; HUF: by law and birth
Sole: unlimited; HUF: only Karta unlimited
Neither is a separate legal entity

narration.en: Both forms are easy to run and are found mainly in small businesses. A sole proprietorship is formed by the will of one person; an HUF business arises by operation of Hindu law. The sole trader has unlimited liability; in an HUF only the Karta does, while coparceners are liable only to the extent of their share. An HUF continues after the death of the Karta, giving it more stability, but the Karta's dominance and limited capital are drawbacks. Neither has a separate legal entity.

explanation.en: Birth and the Karta mark an HUF; one individual owner marks a sole proprietorship; both are simple and not separate legal persons.

problem.en: A sole trader's business has debts of ₹10 lakh and assets of ₹6 lakh. His personal property is worth ₹8 lakh. How much do creditors recover from his personal property?

steps.en: With unlimited liability, creditors can claim the ₹4 lakh from personal property.
He is left with ₹8 lakh − ₹4 lakh = ₹4 lakh.

answer.en: ₹4 lakh is recovered from his personal property.
